result.answer:
## Answer: Yes, you will need to pay the fee again — this time.

Based on your situation (this is your **second** approved-claim incident within 12 months, since March counts as your first), the repeat-claimant fee waiver **has not been met yet**.

**The rule:**
> "Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee." — *Claims FAQ* ([/claims/faq/#fee-waivers](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/faq/))

The waiver requires **two or more prior approved claims** (i.e., you'd need to be filing your *third* incident) — you currently have one prior approved claim (March), so this second claim will still require the standard **¥12,000 claim assessment fee**, payable when the claim is lodged (per the [Claim Fee Schedule](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/fees/)).

**Silver lining:** if your final award for this claim exceeds ¥1,000,000, the ¥12,000 fee is refunded in full — "The assessment fee is refunded in full where the final award exceeds ¥1,000,000." — *Claim Fee Schedule* (/claims/fees/)

**What would change this:** If this were your *third* claim within the rolling 12-month window (i.e., you already had two prior approved claims), you'd be exempt from the fee entirely under the repeat-claimant rule above.

A couple of things worth double-checking with your file:
- Confirm your property qualifies under the zone rule: "Claims require verified structural damage to a property in zones 3, 4 or 5" (/claims/eligibility/) — your Zone 4 location at 300m inside the corridor qualifies.
- As a commercial property (Tanaka Bakery), you're also eligible to additionally claim **business interruption** compensation (/claims/damage-compensation/).

checks.label: States the fee IS payable for this claimant
Notices that pending claims do not count toward the threshold
Notes the waiver applies automatically once the threshold is met

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
